reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge lies in distinguishing between data that can be used for calibration (closing lines) versus data that cannot (play-by-play). The historical replay engine is designed to isolate features from outcomes to avoid lookahead bias. This separation enables the use of frozen models to simulate past bets and compute reliability metrics such as Expected Calibration Error (ECE). The engine’s generic structure allows reuse across sports, but NFL-specific coupling introduces risk of data leakage. Closing-line corpora are essential for generating valid calibration targets, while play-by-play datasets provide only covariates. Thus, the system must prioritize acquiring or validating closed-line datasets before attempting calibration of college football models.
